# Data processing

## Setup

```{r}
# Importing and/or installing packages
packageList = c("gemini.R", "httr2", "jsonlite", "dplyr", "purrr", "data.table", "car", "moments", "psych", "pROC")
packageListRequired = packageList[!(packageList %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])]

if (length(packageListRequired) > 0) {
  install.packages(packageListRequired, dependencies = TRUE)
}

lapply(packageList, library, character.only = TRUE)
```

Characteristics taken from data from observation.

```{r}
characteristics <- c("id",
                     "age", "gender", "isMarried", "education", "hasChildren",
                     "drivingExperience", "creditScore", "speedingViolations", "DUIs", "pastAccidents",
                     "vehicleType", "isVehicleBefore2015", "isVehicleOwner",
                     "isClaimRecorded")
```

Gemini API keys are obtained (stored locally), relevant libraries included, and Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite is utilised. Sample code was adapted to incorporate JSON schema.

```{r}
readRenviron("~/.Renviron")
GEMINI_API_KEY <- Sys.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")

projectDirectory = "~/Data/Documents/2026/2026-2/ACTL30004 (Actuarial Statistics)/Assignments/Assignment 2"
projectSchema    <- jsonlite::fromJSON(path.expand(file.path(projectDirectory, "schema.json")), simplifyVector = FALSE)

Gemini_question = function(input) {
  model = "gemini-3.1-flash-lite"
  api_key = GEMINI_API_KEY
  
  if (api_key == "") {
    stop("GEMINI_API_KEY has not been set.")
  }
  
  url = paste0(
    "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/",
    model,
    ":generateContent"
    )
  
  payload <- list(
    contents = list(
      list(
        parts = list(list(text = input))
      )
    ),
    generationConfig = list(
      responseMimeType = "application/json",
      responseSchema   = list(type = "array", items = projectSchema)
    )
  )
  
  response = request(url) |>
    req_headers(
      'x-goog-api-key' = api_key,
      'Content-Type' = "application/json"
    ) |>
    req_body_json(payload) |>
    req_retry(max_tries = 5, backoff = ~ 3) |>
    req_error(body = function(response) {
      paste("API Error: ", resp_body_string(response))
    }) |>
    req_perform()
  
  result = resp_body_json(response, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  parts  = result$candidates[[1]]$content$parts
  
  text_parts <- vapply(parts, function(x) x$text %||% "", character(1))
  raw_output <- paste(text_parts[nzchar(text_parts)], collapse = "\n")
  
  if (!nzchar(raw_output)) {
    stop("Gemini returned no text response.")
  }
  
  parsed <- tibble::as_tibble(jsonlite::fromJSON(raw_output, simplifyVector = TRUE, flatten = TRUE))
  
  if (!is.null(characteristics)) {
    missingCols <- setdiff(characteristics, names(parsed))
    if (length(missingCols) > 0) {
      parsed[missingCols] <- NA
    }
    parsed <- parsed[, characteristics]
  }
  
  return(parsed)
}
```

Test if API responds and if schema JSON works (both).

```{r}
Gemini_question('Extract driver covariates from each entry into a JSON array in the exact same order: "The driver is a female aged sixtyfive+. They are single, and have a high school degree, with children. They have less than 9 years driving experience, and they own a sedan manufactured after 2015 . During the policy year, the policyholder had no speeding violations, no DUIs and no past accidents. Their credit score is 0.629. No insurance claim was recorded during the policy year."')
```

## Extraction from unstructured text

First row (non-entry) is removed from raw data (text vector), all characteristics (by inspection) are extracted and listed below, and data frame is initialised. Response variable is `isClaimRecorded`.

```{r}
data.raw <- read.csv("data.csv")[[1]]
df.raw   <- data.frame(
  id               = seq_along(data.raw),
  text             = data.raw,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

df <- data.frame(id = df.raw$id)

for (col in setdiff(characteristics, "id")) {
  df[[col]] <- NA
}
```

Declare parameters and functions used in LLM API raw data chunking.

```{r}
entryCount   = length(data.raw)

chunkSize    = 20
chunks <- split(
  df.raw,
  ceiling(seq_len(entryCount) / chunkSize)
)

writeChunkPrompt <- function(chunk) {
  paste0(
    "Extract unstructured insurance data from each entry below (indexed per 'id' number) into a structured JSON.\n",
    "Return only the JSON as specified for the given text, in the order prescribed by the JSON.\n",
    "Do not omit or merge entries.\n",
    paste(
      sprintf("ID %d: %s", chunk$id, chunk$text),
      collapse = "\n"
    )
  )
}
```

Test one chunk.

```{r}
testChunk <- chunks[[1]]

testPrompt <- paste0(
  "Extract unstructured insurance data from each entry below (indexed per 'id' number) into a structured JSON.\n",
  "Return only the JSON as specified for the given text, in the order prescribed by the JSON.\n",
  "Do not omit or merge entries.\n",
  paste(
    sprintf("ID %d: %s", testChunk$id, testChunk$text),
    collapse = "\n"
  )
)

testResult <- Gemini_question(testPrompt)
testResult
```

## Preparation as claims data for analysis

```{r}
claims <- read.csv("claims.csv")

# Remove ID
claims <- claims[, -1]

# LLM appeared to occasionally assert missing credit score as 0 (none in data are strictly 0), change these to NA
claims$creditScore[claims$creditScore == 0] <- NA

# Check NAs
predictorsNA <- sapply(1:13, function(x) { length(which(is.na(claims[, x]))) })
names(predictorsNA) <- names(claims)[1:13]

# 788 entries appear to be missing for credit score, important in just a sec
predictorsNA

# Encode two-level categorical variables as binary
claims$gender <- ifelse(claims$gender == "female", 1, 0)
claims$vehicleType <- ifelse(claims$vehicleType == "sports car", 1, 0)

# Encode remaining categorical variables as factors
claims$age               <- as.factor(claims$age)
claims$education         <- as.factor(claims$education)
claims$drivingExperience <- as.factor(claims$drivingExperience)
```

## Model fitting (via GLM)

Fit full model via GLM. Initially apply to dataset with NAs culled.

```{r}
claims.culled = claims[-which(is.na(claims$creditScore)), ]

# Fit with creditScore (full model)
model.full <- glm(isClaimRecorded ~ age + gender + education + drivingExperience + vehicleType + isMarried + hasChildren + isVehicleBefore2015 + isVehicleOwner + creditScore + speedingViolations + DUIs + pastAccidents,
             family = binomial(link = "logit"),
             data = claims.culled)
```

Investigate whether creditScore should be removed, its NAs may be problematic. Use same dataset as before.

```{r}
# Fit without creditScore
model.noCredit <- glm(isClaimRecorded ~ age + gender + education + drivingExperience + vehicleType + isMarried + hasChildren + isVehicleBefore2015 + isVehicleOwner + speedingViolations + DUIs + pastAccidents,
             family = binomial(link = "logit"),
             data = claims.culled)

# Observe that creditScore is not a strong predictor and the only source of NAs, reasonable to exclude (not associated with other variables where PCA doesn't need to be performed etc)
summary(model.noCredit)

anova(model.noCredit, model.full, test = "Chisq")

model <- glm(isClaimRecorded ~ age + gender + education + drivingExperience + vehicleType + isMarried + hasChildren + isVehicleBefore2015 + isVehicleOwner + speedingViolations + DUIs + pastAccidents,
             family = binomial(link = "logit"),
             data = claims)

```

Check for multicollinearity via VIF.

```{r}
vif(model)
KMO(claims[, c("speedingViolations", "DUIs", "pastAccidents")])
```

Stepwise variable selection performed backwards, using both AIC/BIC as its selection criteria separately. LRT test is performed correspondingly.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
stepwiseAIC <- step(model, direction = "backward", k = 2, trace = 0)
stepwiseBIC <- step(model, direction = "backward", k = log(nrow(claims)), trace = 0)
summary(stepwiseAIC)
summary(stepwiseBIC)

anova(stepwiseAIC, model, test = "Chisq")
anova(stepwiseBIC, model, test = "Chisq")

model <- glm(isClaimRecorded ~ gender + drivingExperience + isMarried + hasChildren + isVehicleBefore2015 + isVehicleOwner + pastAccidents,
             family = binomial(link = "logit"),
             data = claims)
```

## Diagnostics

The following diagnostics are performed (related to assumptions of the final selected GLM):

Overdispersion via deviance dispersion ratio

```{r}
residuals.deviance <- residuals(model, type = "deviance")
residuals.pearson  <- residuals(model, type = "pearson")

dispersionRatio    <- summary(model)$deviance / summary(model)$df.residual
dispersionRatio
```

Leverage, Cook's distance

```{r}
leverageValues     <- hatvalues(model)
cooksDistance      <- cooks.distance(model)

hlpThreshold       <- 3 * (length(coef(model)) - 1 + 1) / nrow(claims)
cooksThreshold     <- 4 / nrow(claims)

highLeverage       <- which(leverageValues > hlpThreshold)
length(highLeverage)
max(leverageValues[highLeverage])

highInfluence      <- which(cooksDistance  > cooksThreshold)
length(highInfluence)
max(cooksDistance)
```

In-sample/out-of-sample ROC-AUC and Brier scores (obtained by taking 70%-30% split of training-test data)

```{r}
set.seed(1)
trainSample  <- sample(nrow(df), nrow(df) * 0.7)

claims.train <- claims[ trainSample, ]
claims.test  <- claims[-trainSample, ]

model.test <- glm(isClaimRecorded ~ gender + drivingExperience + isMarried + hasChildren + isVehicleBefore2015 + isVehicleOwner + pastAccidents,
             family = binomial(link = "logit"),
             data = claims.train)

predictions <- predict(model, newdata = claims.test, type = "response")

rocScore <- roc(claims.test$isClaimRecorded, predictions)
auc(rocScore)

brierScore <- mean((claims.test$isClaimRecorded - predictions)^2)
brierScore
```

Relevant diagnostic plots

```{r, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 10}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), cex = 0.8)

plot(leverageValues, type = "h", main = "Leverage (h_ii)", ylab = "h_ii")
abline(h = hlpThreshold, col = "green")

plot(cooksDistance, type = "h", main = "Cook's Distance", ylab = "Cook's Distance")
abline(h = cooksThreshold, col = "blue")
```

  claims$drivingExperience
